title: spotLight
body:
## spotLight

Creates a SpotLight3D: a cone of light from position along the node's rotated -Z axis, with angle as the cone's half-angle and range as its reach in metres. attenuation and angleAttenuation shape the fall-off with distance and towards the cone edge; shadows can be enabled. Choose it for key lights, stage lights or torches; use omniLight for light in all directions.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- With rotation [0, 0, 0] the cone points horizontally along -Z; aim it with a negative X angle (downward) and a Y angle (heading).
- angle is measured from the cone axis to its edge, so 45 gives a 90-degree wide cone.

Native binding: `SpotLight3D`. Output kind: `["light"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | World position [x, y, z] of the cone apex in metres, the point the light shines from. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":-100000,"maximum":100000},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `rotation` | Aim of the spot light as Euler angles [x, y, z] in degrees (Godot YXZ order), written to rotation_degrees. The cone axis is the node's rotated -Z axis: the X angle tilts it (negative points downward) and the Y angle sets its heading; the Z angle only rolls the cone about its own axis. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":-180,"maximum":180},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `colour` | Colour of the light as [red, green, blue], each 0 to 1, written to light_color (non-linear sRGB in Godot). | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `energy` | Brightness multiplier of the spot light, written to light_energy; Godot states it is not a physical unit. It changes intensity only, not the reach (range) or cone width (angle). | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":16}` | `1` |
| `range` | Maximum distance in metres the cone reaches along its axis, written to spot_range. Surfaces beyond it receive no light from this spot. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0.001,"maximum":100000}` | `5` |
| `attenuation` | Shape of the brightness fall-off with distance along the cone, written to spot_attenuation. As for omni lights, values near 0 keep brightness nearly constant until the edge of range, and 2 gives physically accurate inverse-square fall-off. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0.001,"maximum":16}` | `1` |
| `angle` | Half-angle of the cone in degrees, written to spot_angle: the angle from the cone axis to its edge. The lit cone is twice this wide, so the default 45 lights a 90-degree cone. Schemaxis accepts 1 to 89 degrees. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1,"maximum":89}` | `45` |
| `angleAttenuation` | Shape of the brightness fall-off from the cone axis towards its edge, written to spot_angle_attenuation. Godot documents it as the angular attenuation curve; changing it changes how soft or hard the edge of the light pool looks. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0.001,"maximum":16}` | `1` |
| `shadows` | When true, the spot light casts real-time shadows (Light3D shadow_enabled), so objects in the cone block light from surfaces behind them. Godot notes a significant rendering cost. It affects the preview image and running project, not the verified geometry. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
